sections.h2: Where is Orem, Utah, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Orem is a city in Utah County, about 45 miles south of Salt Lake City, near the eastern shore of Utah Lake. It covers 18.57 square miles of land at an elevation of roughly 4,767 feet, and it borders Provo to the east and south, Vineyard to the west and Lindon to the north.

Two roads shape the map. Interstate 15 runs along the west side with four interchanges inside the city, and US 89 (State Street) cuts through the middle on a northwest to southeast line. Cross streets such as 800 North (Canyon Parkway), 1600 North, University Parkway and Geneva Road carry state route numbers. When a seller in Orem describes a house, buyers usually want to know how far it sits from State Street, University Parkway and the freeway.

sections.h2: How did Orem start, and where does the name come from?
sections.html:
Orem was settled in 1877 and went by Sharon and later Provo Bench before it took its present name. The name came in 1914, honoring Walter C. Orem, president of the Salt Lake and Utah Railroad in the early 1900s, and the town received its charter on May 5, 1919.

Early farmers spread their homes along the territorial highway, which is now State Street, and along other major roads. That pattern still shows. Older lots near State Street and the original grid streets differ a lot from the newer tracts built later. Orem calls itself Family City USA, and its Oremfest celebration dates to 1949, when it marked the completion of State Street.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about housing in Orem?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau counted 98,129 people in Orem in 2020 and estimates 95,214 for July 1, 2025. Orem is the fifth most populous city in Utah, and homeowners make up a little more than half of its households.

These are survey medians for the whole city, not a value for any one house. Condition, lot, and street all move a single sale away from the middle.

sections.h2: What kinds of homes does Orem have?
sections.html:
Orem has a mix of detached houses, townhomes and apartments, and the city publishes the split. Of 29,593 occupied units in the 2021 American Community Survey, 17,913 (60.5%) were owner-occupied and 11,680 (39.5%) were rented.

  • Single-family homes: 16,509 units, or 55.8% of occupied housing
  • Twinhomes and townhomes: 3,227 units, or 10.9%
  • Buildings with 10 or more apartments or condos: 4,434 units, or 15.0%
  • Mobile homes and other types: 575 units, or 1.9%

Among renter-occupied units, 33.8% sit in buildings of ten or more. A house that has been a rental for years may need different handling than an owner-occupied one, because tenants, leases and deferred repairs affect how a sale goes.

sections.h2: What are the rules for accessory apartments in Orem?
sections.html:
Orem allows accessory apartments inside a main home, but the owner has to live in either the main residence or the apartment. The city counted 752 legal accessory apartments as of June 2023, with 30 added in 2022 and 23 more in the first half of 2023.

That owner-occupancy rule matters when you sell. A basement apartment that was never registered, or one that a prior owner rented while living elsewhere, can be a problem for a conventional buyer's lender and inspector. Detached units are a newer topic. A Herald Extra report from July 2026 said Orem had not allowed detached accessory dwellings before, and that the city's proposed response to state law S.B. 284 would keep them out of front yards and bar short-term rental use. The statute, as that article describes it, applies to lots of 11,000 square feet or more and required cities to amend their policies by October 1.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers near Orem homes?
sections.html:
Utah Valley University is Orem's largest employer by a wide margin, with 3,030 employees, or 5.9% of city employment, in the city's 2023 financial report. The ten largest employers together account for 7,793 jobs, about 15.3% of the city total.

  • Utah Valley University: 3,030
  • Alpine School District: 1,222
  • City of Orem: 569
  • Timpanogos Regional Hospital: 507
  • Avetta, LLC: 500
  • Walmart: 499
  • Target: 409
  • United Parcel Service: 360
  • Costco: 350
  • U.S. Synthetic Corporation: 347

UVU enrolled more than 43,000 undergraduates as of late 2022, which is why rental demand near campus is part of the Orem housing story. Orem also has a technology history: Novell, WordPerfect, Omniture and Blendtec all started here.

sections.h2: How do people get around Orem?
sections.html:
Orem has a FrontRunner commuter rail station on the west side of I-15, linked to the UVU campus by a pedestrian bridge. UVX, a bus rapid transit line run jointly with Provo, connects Orem Central Station, UVU and University Parkway toward Provo.

The average commute for Orem workers is 20.1 minutes. Homes within walking distance of the station or a UVX stop can talk about that in a listing, but the rail line also brings freight and train noise that a buyer may weigh the other way. Geneva Road, which runs near the former steel mill site just west of the city, has changed a lot as that land has been redeveloped.

sections.h2: Which school district serves Orem, and what changes in 2027?
sections.html:
Alpine School District serves Orem today, and it will be dissolved on July 1, 2027. Orem is assigned to the new Timpanogos district, along with Pleasant Grove, Lindon and Vineyard, according to the June 2026 resource agreement reported by the Herald Extra.

Voters approved the split in the 2024 general election, board members were elected in 2025, and superintendents were hired in 2026. Buyers with school-age children often ask which district a house belongs to, so the answer for an Orem listing is changing in the middle of the sale year. Utah State University also runs an education center in Orem.

sections.h2: How does property tax work for an Orem house?
sections.html:
Utah County bills Orem property taxes. Owners get a Notice of Property Valuation and Tax Changes near the end of July, and market-value appeals go to the county Board of Equalization, with a filing deadline of September 15.

The tax notice itself arrives between the middle and end of October. Primary homes get a 45% residential exemption, so tax is calculated on 55% of market value, provided the home is occupied at least 183 consecutive days in a year by the owner, a family member or a full-time tenant. A rental that is not occupied full-time by an eligible occupant counts as secondary and is taxed on full value.

A change of ownership can trigger a declaration form for the new owner. Questions about payoffs go to the Utah County Treasurer at 801-851-8255, and the county Recorder at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300 in Provo handles recording of the deed. The recorder's office does not prepare documents, give legal advice or run title searches.

sections.h2: Does earthquake risk change how an Orem sale works?
sections.html:
Orem sits in a seismic region, and buyers sometimes ask about it. The Wasatch Fault runs about 240 miles with ten segments, five of them active, and the Provo segment is among the active ones. The last large event on the Provo segment was roughly 200 to 700 years ago, and about 80% of Utah residents live along the fault.

Nothing in Utah law makes a seller fix a house for that risk. A buyer's inspector may still note chimney bracing, water heater straps and foundation ties, so older brick homes can draw more questions.

sections.h2: What do Orem sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale work here?
sections.html:
Orem sellers most often deal with an inherited house, a rental that needs work, a basement apartment without paperwork, or a move on a tight date. A cash sale to us follows a short path: you tell us about the property, we look at it, and we make an offer based on its condition.

We buy as-is, so you do not paint, patch or clean before a closing. The closing runs through a title or escrow company, and the deed is recorded with the Utah County Recorder. If the offer does not suit you, you can decline it and owe nothing.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Orem house if it has an unregistered basement apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. Orem requires the owner to live in the main home or the apartment, so a conventional buyer's lender or inspector may raise questions. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, which avoids that hurdle.

faqs.q: How long does Utah County take to record a deed for an Orem sale?
faqs.a: The Utah County Recorder accepts and records documents that meet state requirements. The title or escrow company usually submits the deed, so you rarely deal with the office yourself. Ask your closing agent about timing.

faqs.q: Does a tenant in my Orem house stop me from selling?
faqs.a: No. A tenant does not block a sale. A buyer takes the property subject to the lease unless the tenant leaves, so tell us about any lease and the move-out date when you reach out.

faqs.q: Which school district will Orem homes belong to after 2027?
faqs.a: Orem is assigned to the new Timpanogos district once Alpine School District is dissolved on July 1, 2027. Check the district boundary map for your exact address.

faqs.q: When is the deadline to appeal an Orem property valuation?
faqs.a: Utah County sets September 15 as the deadline to file an appeal for any reason. A late appeal can be filed through March 31 if it meets extra criteria and the Board of Equalization accepts it.
